goal: Hook: listen to the quiet tune and sudden loud chord of Haydn's "Surprise" movement and pose the question; teach the circle, the quiet signal and the sound rules.

goal: Teach the steady beat with its step card: pat it on the knees, then walk it in place; teach the stick tub routine (out by rows, back by rows, about 3 minutes).

goal: Teach the singing voice with the soft siren slide step card, and show high and low with the hands as the voice slides up and down.
note: Voice: no shouting, soft short slides, no child sings alone, water and voice rest.

goal: Beat-keeping rounds and pitch-matching slides in short echoes, with feedback; begin the baseline look at the main look-for (a steady beat) in rotating groups.

goal: Teach loud and soft and same and different with the body (big and small moves, the same-or-different sign) in the class songs.

goal: Listen again to Haydn: pat the beat, then trace the tune stepping up and down with a hand; name its maker, place and time.
note: Recordings at the set low level the class can talk over; quiet rest after loud music; hearing protection or a quiet seat allowed.

goal: Teach what music goes with: match the quiet tune to a tiptoe-story picture, then choose among four card kinds, one for each part: another art (a story), a school subject (a counting song), a setting (a place) and daily life (a game or a time of day).
note: Picture cards are Curio Class's own.

goal: Listen to the Yoruba dùndún talking drum on a museum or sound archive page: hear its high and low tones, show them with the hands, and learn where and by whom it is played.
note: Sensitivity: the class listens only and does not imitate the drum's speech; the sensitivity agent reads the holding archive's page and a Yoruba drummer's own published words first. Described and linked, never copied. Recordings at the set low level the class can talk over; quiet rest after loud music; hearing protection or a quiet seat allowed.

goal: Echo drills on high and low, loud and soft, and same and different, and "ta" spoken on each patted beat, echoed after the teacher, then a beat round with sticks.
note: "ta" is by ear only: no symbols, nothing scored. Sticks never near a face; knees as the drum on the free path.

goal: Teach judging by taste with the class listening routine (listen, show it, say what you hear, say if you like it and why) and the frame "I like it because it is ___."
note: The describe-interpret-judge routine starts here; a child may show the word instead of saying it.

goal: Teach "Kye Kye Kule" as a call-and-response game song from Ghana: the teacher calls, the class answers, and the class hears what is the same and different between call and answer and where the game is played.

goal: Groups rehearse "Kye Kye Kule" with sticks keeping the beat, choose loud or soft for the call, and make up their own clapped answer for the last line.
note: Creating is practiced here, not claimed. Groups of five. Space: cleared circle, arms out, stepping in place, never running.

goal: Beat and pitch echo drills, with "ti-ti" added for two even sounds on one beat, then each group runs its part of the game song twice.
note: "ti-ti" by ear only: no symbols, nothing scored. Voice: no shouting, soft short slides, no child sings alone, water and voice rest.

goal: Revision: each group makes the one suggested change, rehearses, and says in one line what it changed.

goal: End-of-unit assessment: six groups of five at the teacher's spot (about four minutes each): show three sung pairs with the body, pat eight beats and trace the tune of an unseen Curio Class original, and answer two talk items (a liking with one sound reason; which of four picture cards, one for each part (a story, a counting song, a place, a time of day), the piece goes with and why).
